ops.body:
reposync MERGE STAGE (Run wf_37624322-e25, reposync:merge-fixes): apply reviews/reposync-history-cache-v2.patch INSTEAD of reposync-history-cache.patch.
- v2 = root patch + fix (base 826a351, only worktree/history.go + history_test.go; `git apply --check` OK).
- allPublished uses `cat-file -e` (the same check canAppend uses) instead of `rev-parse --verify --quiet`.
- New test TestCaptureSurfacesUnreadableHistoryPrerequisite fails on v1 and passes on v2: an unreadable loose object now surfaces merge-base's exit-128 error.
- Both root regressions pass (-race -count=3).

Coordinator decision on the second refutation (Run wf_7262c36c-263): with an unreadable pack/.idx or a missing alternates dir, git exits 1 with no stderr, so v2 treats the prerequisite as missing and rebuilds. Accepted, not fixed:
- git exposes no distinguishing signal in one call.
- The rebuilt chain is created, and Complete reported, only if every object it needs is readable (bundle create fails loudly otherwise).
- So the result stays truthful; checking store health is not capture's job.
Root may object here.

Also decided (reposync capture lane):
- L0-8 split-index sharedindex mtime → option (a): git's own freshen_shared_index on every split-index read (git status does the same). Bytes unchanged, no new files. A pinning test plus a Capture godoc line; no private-index machinery, which would also miss submodules.
- L0-3 → option (a): bounded per-commit .gitattributes transitions reusing the historyLFS diff-tree pass; absent objects raise MissingLFSError.
